title: Connect a weighted network
problem: Given a connected undirected graph with positive integer edge costs, output a spanning tree of minimum total cost. The input is an explicit vertex and edge list and the output is the selected edge indices.

title: Select nonoverlapping appointments
problem: Given integer start and finish times for appointments on one resource, select a maximum-cardinality nonoverlapping subset. Every selected appointment occupies its full half-open time interval.

title: Find a route through a network
problem: Given a connected graph with positive integer edge weights and two distinguished vertices, return a minimum-cost path between them as a sequence of adjacent vertices.

title: Assign workers to jobs
problem: Given a bipartite graph listing which workers are eligible for which jobs, assign at most one job per worker and at most one worker per job while maximizing the number of assigned jobs.

title: Encode runs of repeated characters
problem: Given a lowercase string, emit its canonical run-length encoding, representing each maximal consecutive run by its character and positive length. Decoding the result must recover the exact input.

title: Divide a list into equal workloads
problem: Given a list of positive integer jobs and a target load, determine whether some subset sums exactly to the target, and return such a subset when it exists. The target is small enough for exact dynamic programming.

title: Move through a rectangular grid
problem: Given a rectangular grid with nonnegative cell costs, find a minimum-cost path from its top-left to bottom-right corner using only right and down moves. Return the visited cell coordinates.

title: Color a tree
problem: Given a tree, assign one of two colors to each vertex so that the endpoints of every edge have different colors. Return a color for every vertex and preserve the input vertex numbering.

title: Choose a meeting location on a line
problem: Given integer locations and positive integer demand weights on a line, choose one integer meeting location minimizing the sum of weighted absolute distances. Return the location and its total distance.

title: Cover a line segment with intervals
problem: Given intervals with integer endpoints and a target line segment, choose as few intervals as possible whose union covers the target, or report that complete coverage is impossible.

title: Pack integer-valued items
problem: Given items with positive integer weights and values and a small integer capacity, choose a subset of maximum total value whose total weight fits the capacity. Each item can be chosen at most once.

title: Parenthesize matrix multiplication
problem: Given compatible matrix dimensions, choose a parenthesization minimizing the number of scalar multiplications for their product. Matrices must retain their original order.

title: Order dependent build steps
problem: Given a directed acyclic graph of build prerequisites, output a permutation of all steps in which every prerequisite precedes the step that depends on it.

title: Transform one string into another
problem: Given two strings, return a minimum-length edit script using single-character insertions, deletions and substitutions. Executing the script must turn the source string into the target string.

title: Tile an empty rectangle
problem: Given positive integer width and height, cover every cell of the rectangle with unit squares with no gaps or overlaps. Return integer coordinates for each square.

title: Serve requests with a fixed-size cache
problem: Given an offline sequence of object requests and a cache holding a fixed number of equally sized objects, return eviction decisions minimizing the number of misses, starting with an empty cache.

title: Route flow through a network
problem: Given a directed graph with nonnegative integer edge capacities and a source and sink, output a maximum feasible flow respecting edge capacities and conservation at intermediate vertices.

title: Align two symbol sequences
problem: Given two symbol sequences and fixed mismatch and gap costs, return a minimum-cost alignment that preserves the order of each original sequence.

title: Distribute a small resource budget
problem: Given a small integer budget and a table of rewards for allocating each possible number of units to each project, find an allocation maximizing total reward without exceeding the budget.

title: Visit vertices of a tree
problem: Given a weighted tree with a distinguished starting vertex, produce a minimum-length closed walk visiting every vertex at least once, and return its sequence of adjacent vertices.
